prompt.query: Determine the mechanism of the following reaction: Paal-Knorr furan synthesis: 2,5-hexanedione -> 2,5-dimethylfuran + H2O (acid-catalyzed). Reactant SMILES: [OH3+].CC(=O)CCC(C)=O; product SMILES: [OH3+].Cc1ccc(C)o1.O; total charge 1, multiplicity 1; conditions: acid-catalyzed (H3O+ written into the SMILES on both sides; Lewis acid is the classical alternative), heated. Atom-mapped reactant SMILES: [OH2+:9]([H:10]).[CH2:1]([H:11])[C:2](=[O:3])[CH:4]([H:12])[CH:5]([H:13])[C:6](=[O:7])[CH3:8]. The 1-based map numbers in it are the indexing convention for `bond_changes` (keep using the plain SMILES above for graph nodes and evidence annotations). The reaction may proceed through a multi-step network: represent each intermediate you identify as a node and each elementary step as an edge; competing pathways you investigate deserve their own edges. You must maintain `mechanism_graph.json` in the sandbox root recording the mechanism graph: nodes (reactant/intermediate/product/transition_state, with SMILES) and elementary-step edges (with `via` pointing to the TS node id). Start the graph at the reactant complex (the pre-reaction complex), not at the separated reactants. The scorer checks that your graph covers the reference mechanism as a subgraph: extra nodes or edges beyond the reference are never penalized, so record every step you actually investigated. Every elementary-step edge must carry `bond_changes`: `break`/`form` lists of [i, j] atom-map index pairs, where [i, j] belongs to `break` if the bond order between atoms i and j decreases over the step (including full cleavage) and to `form` if it increases (including newly formed bonds); a purely conformational or inversion step carries two empty lists. The scorer reads this file forensically; a missing or unparseable file severely impacts the score. Every computational evidence file you produce for a species or step (QM input or log) must carry a `smiles: <SMILES>` comment line identifying the species, so the scorer can bind each graph element to concrete evidence. In your final summary you must report the computed barrier in kcal/mol for the rate-determining step, relative to the reactant complex (the pre-reaction complex, e.g. the ion-dipole complex of a bimolecular reaction; for a unimolecular process this is simply the reactant minimum). Run the computations with ORCA or Gaussian: the scorer parses only these two programs' log formats, so output from any other program cannot count as evidence. Allowed computational methods are limited to MACE-OMol25 and xTB; calls beyond the whitelist are intercepted.

system.conditions: acid-catalyzed (H3O+ written into the SMILES on both sides; Lewis acid is the classical alternative), heated

edges.step_type: carbonyl oxygen protonation by hydronium (PT, first half of acid-catalyzed enolization)
water deprotonates the alpha carbon: C=O pi shifts to C=C pi and H3O+ is regenerated -> enol (net acid-catalyzed enolization)
intramolecular ring closure of the enol oxygen onto the second carbonyl (cyclization is rate-determining region) with O->O proton transfer -> cyclic hemiketal

dehydration with aromatization: C-OH cleavage, ring pi rearrangement to the aromatic furan, and proton relocations (C5-H to the departing hydroxyl, C4-H to the exocyclic methylene) -> 2,5-dimethylfuran + water (only one water, unlike the pyrrole series)
